s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive back pain with systemic inflammation and neurological deficits
salient_findings: Neurological deficits including weakness, numbness, and difficulty with urination
key_facts: 1-month history of high fever, night sweats, and progressive back pain
Patient touched an unpasteurized sheep stomach with an injured hand about 1 month earlier
Initial outpatient therapy with oral cefprozil provided no lasting benefit
White-cell count of 7170/mm3 with 80% neutrophils
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 35 mm/hour
C-reactive protein level of 3.19 mg/dL
Procalcitonin level of 0.21 ng/mL
Serological test for tuberculosis was negative
Blood cultures grew a Gram-negative bacillus on hospital day 6
Developed weakness and numbness in both legs and difficulty with urination on hospital day 6
Neurologic examination revealed grade 3/5 strength in the right lower limb and grade 4/5 in the left
Hypertonia of both lower extremities and tenderness on percussion and palpation of the T9 and T10 spinous processes
Contrast-enhanced thoracic magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated an inflammatory lesion of the T9 lamina and a posterior epidural abscess compressing the spinal cord at T9–T10

shortlist.why_kept: Patient touched an unpasteurized sheep stomach with an injured hand, which is a risk factor for brucellosis, and has symptoms consistent with the disease

shortlist.why_kept: Patient has progressive back pain, systemic inflammation, and neurological deficits, with imaging showing an inflammatory lesion, which could be consistent with spinal tuberculosis
